learning_outcomes.text: Know the main theoretical and applicative aspects of Fluid Mechanics, and understand the techniques of analysis of problems in Fluid Mechanics, paying attention to the differences between models and real behavior of the physical processes.

Be able to describe the physical process by using applied mathematics; to select the parameters and the variables involved in the process; to solve the most common applicative cases checking the results with an engineering approach.
Be able to evaluate the reliability of simplified models or the need to adopt advanced models.
Be able to clearly present the results of the analysis, in oral or written form, also by means of tables and charts.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to vector fields and to differential operators, to tensors
Definition of fluid as a continuum
Fluid mechanics variables and units of measurement
Internal stresses in fluids at rest
Finite control volume analysis of fluid statics
Hydrostatic force on plane and curved surfaces
Differential and finite control volume analyses of a fluid flow
The differential equation of linear momentum
Examples of the use of the Bernoulli equation
Extension of the use of the Bernoulli equation to streams
Analytical solutions of the Navier-Stokes equations: Couette flow, Hagen-Poiseuille flow
teaching_methods: Frontal lessons on the blackboard (with the projection of slides and video educational)

assessment_methods.method: Theory questions, applications of theory, presentation ability

assessment_rules: The examination is based on a written exam consisting of numerical exercises and theory questions. Exercises account for 50% of the evaluation, and theory questions, applications of theory, and presentation ability account for the remaining 50%.
